Failure during drop to unmap persistent carrier stage-2 mappings leaves dangling stage-2 translations referencing freed host memory. Re-reviewed 2026-08-31: the abort itself is unchanged; the surrounding function was edited (alias state partitioned by ownership scope and indexed, page-table pre-images journalled instead of cloned), which is what moved the fingerprint.

Retiring a persistent carrier stage-2 lease failed at the carrier authority's terminal point, after which the `OwnedHostMapping` below releases the host backing. Continuing would leave the guest a live stage-2 route into freed host memory, so this is the same condition -- and the same verdict -- as the `hv_vm_unmap` failure in the lease-less branch of this very loop, which has always aborted here (ordinal #1). It restores the abort that lease `Drop` performed before `901945f82` moved retirement to explicit safe points.

The alias version chain named by a retiring version id was absent from the keyed chain map. retire_exact now finds a chain through alias_version_owner (an id -> key index) instead of scanning every chain's version list, so an id present in the index with no chain behind it is a torn alias-version registry, not a lookup miss. Aborting keeps the previous behaviour of the unwrap_or_else(abort) this replaced.
As #5 for the REPLAY half: a version id present in replay_version_owner whose ReplayVersionChain is missing means the replay version registry and its index disagree.
